players.product: data-center communications infrastructure (design, build, maintenance) and generator enclosures used in data centers

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Simmes: for fiscal 2025 (ended September 30, 2025) IES reported approximate revenue of $3.4 billion, operating income of $384 million and adjusted EPS of $13.66, with over 170 locations and over 11,000 employees; over the past five years revenue grew at a 23% compound annual growth rate and operating income at 50%, with operating margins rising from just under 4% to over 11%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue ~$3.4 billion; operating income $384 million; revenue 23% CAGR over five years

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Simmes: two years ago more than half of IES revenue came from the residential segment, falling to 39% in 2025 and tracking under 30% year to date in 2026, driven partly by housing-start slowdowns but more by rapid growth of other markets, particularly data centers; data-center capital spending for generative AI and cloud is currently the largest growth driver for the Communications, Infrastructure Solutions and Commercial & Industrial segments.
quarterly_data.figure: residential 39% of revenue in 2025; under 30% year to date in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Tracy McLauchlin: operating income for the first nine months ended June 30, 2026 was $389 million, a 39% increase over the same period of 2025, driven largely by Communications and Infrastructure Solutions and by expanded Commercial & Industrial capabilities in the data center space; Commercial & Industrial revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 more than doubled over the same quarter of 2025 after two years of hiring and training to expand capacity for large data center projects.
quarterly_data.figure: 9M FY2026 operating income $389 million, +39%; C&I quarterly revenue doubled

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Tracy McLauchlin: IES expects the strengths and weaknesses seen in the third quarter and the first nine months to continue for the rest of the fiscal year, with Communications and Infrastructure Solutions leading the way; in multifamily, the backlog decline of 2024 and 2025 has stabilized and the sales pipeline is improving, with new work benefiting from 2027.
CFO Tracy McLauchlin: IES exited the June 30 quarter with record backlog, which it expects will drive further growth heading into fiscal 2027.

CFO Tracy McLauchlin: in Infrastructure Solutions (generator enclosures, switchgear, bus duct), the Gulf Island acquisition completed in January contributed $89 million of revenue for the nine months ended June 30; excluding it, the segment's year-to-date growth rate of 57% was 32% organic. IES now has approximately 3 million square feet of manufacturing space, roughly a third still being redeveloped or retooled and likely to contribute from fiscal 2027; CEO Matt Simmes: that capacity is sold out, it is one of IES's highest-margin businesses, and custom enclosures for data-center backup generators are its largest growth driver; Chinese competition can affect cost and margins but demand is outpacing those risks.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 3 million square feet of manufacturing space, sold out; Gulf Island $89 million 9M revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Simmes: the amount of fiber IES installs in data centers today is 10X what it put in four years ago, because data centers are now interwoven fabrics rather than copper point-to-point links and campus buildings need far larger interconnections - some fiber optic cables cost $2 million, $3 million a piece; data-center growth is probably an even split between price and volume, as labor rates have grown dramatically; IES performs day-to-day data-center operations (rack and stack, patching, network turn up) as well as construction, and its project visibility has never been longer.
quarterly_data.figure: fiber installed per data center 10X vs four years ago; some cables $2 million, $3 million a piece

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Simmes: IES has agreed to acquire DBM Global, its largest acquisition to date, a structural steel fabrication business with 3,400 employees that will add a fifth operating segment and that works with many large general contractors already IES customers; closing is expected in the quarter ending December 31, 2026, pending regulatory approval.
quarterly_data.figure: 3,400 employees; close expected quarter ending December 31, 2026
